PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
Machine Learning Engineer
Osijek, Croatia | petra.zlataric@example.com | +385 55 555 0606 | github.com/pzn-ml-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine learning engineer with more than five years of experience in natural language processing and document classification, from research and prototyping to production models. Experienced in transformer fine-tuning, model serving and production monitoring on Azure. Doctoral researcher in Croatian language processing.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Machine Learning Engineer | Slavonica Document AI d.o.o. | Osijek
03/2023–Present
- Developed an automated document classification model for public administration clients, achieving 94% accuracy across 23 classes, including invoices, contracts and official decisions.
- Fine-tuned BERTić and XLM-R transformer models for named entity recognition in Croatian documents.
- Introduced MLflow for experiment tracking and the model registry; models are delivered as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service.
- Established production model quality monitoring, including data drift monitoring and weekly reporting.
- Mentor two student interns.

Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka d.d. | Zagreb, remote from Osijek
09/2021–02/2023
- Built customer churn prediction models using gradient boosting and LightGBM for the sales team.
- Classified topics in customer complaint texts using TF-IDF and logistic regression, later using fastText.
- Produced SQL reports using an Oracle data warehouse.

Research Project Assistant | Faculty of Applied Informatics, University of Drava
10/2020–08/2021
- Built and annotated a corpus of Croatian legal texts and wrote Python scripts.

EDUCATION

Doctoral Studies in Computer Science | University of Drava | 2022–Present
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts

Master of Computer Engineering (Mag. ing. comp.) | University of Drava | 2020

SKILLS
Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, Git, Linux

LANGUAGES
Croatian: Native | English: C1 | German: B2

PUBLICATIONS
Zlatarić-Novosel, P. et al. (2024). Named entity recognition for Croatian administrative documents. Workshop on Slavic language processing (fictional proceedings).

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is concise, well structured, professionally written, and easy to scan. It presents a clear machine learning profile, relevant NLP experience, production deployment work, Azure experience, and a strong quantified achievement (94% accuracy across 23 classes). The reverse-chronological experience section is effective, and the education, skills, language, and publication sections are complete. The main content limitation is that several production-engineering activities relevant to this role—such as data ingestion pipelines, feature engineering, automated testing, CI/CD, and integration with broader product systems—are not demonstrated. These are alignment limitations rather than defects that can be solved without additional supporting experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional text formatting, readable date ranges, explicit technology names, and no problematic tables, graphics, headers, or multi-column layout. Strong searchable terms include Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML, App Service, model registry, model serving, monitoring, data drift, SQL, LightGBM, and NLP. ATS screening probability is strong for general Machine Learning Engineer and NLP/production ML roles. Screening probability for this specific role will be reduced by the absence of truthful evidence or keywords for chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), data ingestion pipelines, feature engineering, automated testing, CI/CD, and orchestration beyond MLflow.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the degree requirement, Python, Azure, MLflow/MLOps, model serving, production monitoring, transformer fine-tuning, language-model-related work, and customer-support-adjacent text classification. It also demonstrates relevant financial-services experience through churn prediction, customer complaint classification, and Oracle data reporting. The document shows more than five years of ML/NLP experience and production-model work, but it does not clearly establish four full years specifically shipping ML systems in production; the detailed production deployment evidence is concentrated in the current role. The candidate's material does not show experience with chat assistants or RAG, feature engineering, data ingestion pipelines, CI/CD, automated tests, or data versioning, so these are genuine alignment gaps and should not be implied. The CV does not currently provide evidence directly related to the company's teamwork, ownership, pragmatism, or learning-culture signals, although mentoring and production ownership provide some adjacent evidence.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the production engineering keywords more explicit without increasing the claimed experience duration. For example, change the final sentence to: "Experienced in transformer fine-tuning, model serving, model registries, production monitoring, and Azure ML deployment." All of these capabilities are supported by the current CV.
2. In the current Machine Learning Engineer role, revise the MLflow bullet to include the ATS term "MLOps" while preserving the factual detail: "Introduced MLflow as an MLOps practice for experiment tracking and model registry; deployed models as FastAPI services in Docker containers on Azure ML and App Service." 
3. In the current Machine Learning Engineer role, make the operational ownership clearer by changing "Established production model quality monitoring, including data drift monitoring and weekly reporting" to "Established production model-quality monitoring, including data-drift monitoring and weekly quality reporting." This makes the monitoring scope easier for recruiters and ATS systems to identify without adding unsupported claims.
4. In the Skills section, group the existing skills under simple ATS-readable labels rather than leaving them as one undifferentiated list. For example: "Programming: Python, SQL"; "ML/NLP: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, scikit-learn, LightGBM, fastText, spaCy"; "MLOps and Deployment: MLflow, FastAPI, Docker, Azure ML"; "Data and Systems: pandas, NumPy, Git, Linux." Do not add tools or capabilities not present in the current CV.
